messages:
julie (Support): FYI customer reported intermittent invalid JSON from JSON mode. Happening on hosted, spikes ~1-2% of requests since yesterday evening. They say fields from other responses are appearing in the JSON output.
sam (eng-runtime): Can you paste an example of the corrupted output + the request metadata (model, session id, request id)?
julie (Support): Sure, truncated example below. customer says pattern is when they have many concurrent short requests on the same session (session header used for KV/prefix caching).

Corrupt response (observed):
```
{"id": "resp_123", "items": [{"name": "widget", "qty": 3}], "meta": {"trace": "abc..."}, "prev": {"name": "cached_item", "qty": 1}}
```
Expected (correct):
```
{"id": "resp_123", "items": [{"name": "widget", "qty": 3}], "meta": {"trace": "abc..."}}
```
Notes: the extra `prev` object looks like it was copied from a prior response in the same session.
Request headers: model: rwd-7b-hf, json_mode: structured, session-id: sess-77a2, batching: enabled, prefix_cache: enabled
Request id: req_20260317_001

Customer repro claim: when they fire 8 concurrent requests with small prompt sizes (~20 tokens) using the same session-id, ~1 in 50 responses has fields mixed in.

riley (Support): Adding logs and traces below from their session forwarded via support upload.
```
[2026-03-16T22:15:12.123Z] req=req_... sess=sess-77a2 batch=slot-3 tokenstream=partial::{"id":"resp_122","items":[{"name":"foo","qty":2}]}
[2026-03-16T22:15:12.124Z] req=req_... sess=sess-77a2 cache_write=slot-3 done
[2026-03-16T22:15:12.125Z] req=req_... sess=sess-77a2 batch=slot-4 tokenstream=partial::{"id":"resp_123","items":[{"name":"widget","qty":3}]}
[2026-03-16T22:15:12.126Z] req=req_... sess=sess-77a2 merge=slot-3->slot-4 kv_merge=ok
```
sam (eng-runtime): Huh — logs show `merge=slot-3->slot-4` right when slot-4 is being emitted. That smells like a race in the batch-to-session merge logic where buffered KV/prefix state from one batch is being appended during streaming. Could be an ordering bug in the session cache flush.
mora (eng-ml): Likely root cause: when streaming structured JSON, token boundaries align with fields. If one stream finishes and its KV is flushed while another stream is concurrently being emitted, we might accidentally interleave buffered tokens. Especially with small prompts and high concurrency the batching window is tiny but flush/merge still fires.
sam (eng-runtime): Checklist: 1) reproduce locally with same concurrency & same session id; 2) add epoch/sequence markers on emitted token fragments to validate ordering; 3) add a short-term guard: disallow cross-batch prefix merges while a streaming emission is in-progress for the same session.
julie (Support): Customer is asking for a quick mitigation — they can’t disable structured mode. Any quick toggles we can suggest?
riley (Support): Suggested workaround sent: set header `X-Prefix-Cache: disabled` or use unique session-id per request. Sent to customer as temporary. They applied `X-Prefix-Cache: false` and reported much lower incidence in initial QA (0/500 concurrent hits).
mora (eng-ml): For a proper fix we should: 1) ensure session-level locks for streaming emissions OR 2) atomically attach KV deltas to the end of the correct response stream rather than via a shared merge path. Also add a regression test in the eval harness that runs many concurrent short JSON-mode requests sharing a session id.
sam (eng-runtime): I ran a quick local repro script and reproduced ~1/120 failure rate with 12 concurrent requests sharing session-id. Repro script (python):
```
import requests, threading
URL='https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate'
HEADERS={'Authorization':'Bearer x', 'Content-Type':'application/json', 'X-Session-Id':'sess-race'}
PAYLOAD={"model":"rwd-7b-ff", "json_mode": true, "prompt": "{\"op\":\"list\"}"}
results=[]
def call():
  r=requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json=PAYLOAD, timeout=10)
  results.append(r.text)
threads=[threading.Thread(target=call) for _ in range(12)]
for t in threads: t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()
# check for stray keys across results
```
I can share logs and tracers to match their req IDs.

sam (eng-runtime): Created a quick PR branch that adds sequence ids to fragment emissions and a mutex around session-level merges: r/eng-runtime/patch/session-merge-guard. Running CI & stress tests now. If that passes we can hotfix on hosted.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline for r/eng-runtime/patch/session-merge-guard started: job/5482.

mora (eng-ml): Also add a small change to the structured JSON serializer: always close object boundaries before writing any cached prefix attachments. This guards against partial field bleed when tokenization splits inside field names/values.
riley (Support): Escalating to Priority 2 for hosted customers. Notified accounts team. Customer impact: intermittent invalid JSON leading to parsing errors on their end (some 500s and retries), they reported an uptick in error budget incidents.
julie (Support): Next actions: 1) eng-runtime to confirm repro branch results and provide ETA for hotfix; 2) eng-ml to add serializer guard and regression tests; 3) support to keep customer on the workaround or recommend unique session ids if possible.
sam (eng-runtime): Will aim to have a hotfix candidate in the next 6-8 hours if stress passes. I'll post back with job/5482 result and links to a canary rollout plan (canary = a single region + subset of tenants).
julie (Support): thanks — will hold customer's hand for the workaround until we patch. :pray:
